questions.question: A sum of Rs 2,432 amounts to Rs 2,681.28 in 2 years at a certain rate percent per annum, interest compounded yearly. What will be simple interest (in Rs) on the same sum for \(4\frac{3}{8}\) years at double the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs 2,432 amounts to Rs 2,681.28 in 2 years at a certain rate percent per annum, interest compounded yearly. What will be simple interest (in Rs) on the same sum for \(4\frac{3}{8}\) years at double the same rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rs. 2,432 amounts to Rs.2,681.28 in 2 years 

Formulas used:

When the interest is compounded annually 

A = P (1 + r/100)n

Simple interest = P × R/100 × Time 

Calculation:

A = P (1 + r/100)n

⇒ 2681.28 = 2432 (1 + r/100)2

⇒ 2681.28/2432 = [(100 + r)/100]2

⇒ 441/400 = [(100 + r)/100]2

√441/400 = (100 + r)/100

⇒ 21/20 = (100 + r)/100

⇒ 105 = 100 + r 

⇒ r = 5%

Simple Interest on Rs.2432 at 10% p.a. for \(4\frac{3}{8}\) years. 

⇒ SI = 2432 × 10/100 × 35/8 

∴ Simple interest = Rs.1064

questions.question: A man invested ₹4,500 at 5% per annum and ₹5,500 at 8% per annum simple interest. Both investments were for 4 years each. The amount received from the lower rate of interest is what per cent (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the amount received from the higher rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A man invested ₹4,500 at 5% per annum and ₹5,500 at 8% per annum simple interest. Both investments were for 4 years each. The amount received from the lower rate of interest is what per cent (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the amount received from the higher rate of interest?
questions.solution:
The simple interest got by the person is   ⇒  4500 × 5 × 4 / 100 = 900

The simple interest got by the person is   ⇒  5500 × 8 × 4 / 100 = 1760

​% of lower SI w.r.t. higher SI will be (900/1760) × 100 ⇒ 51% 
But ​% of lower and higher amounts =(5400/7260) × 100
= 74%

questions.question: A man invested a total of Rs.12,050 in two parts, one at 10% p.a. simple interest for 2 years and the other at the same rate at compound interest, interest being compounded annually, for the same time. The amounts he received from both the parts are equal. The sum (in Rs.) invested at the compound interest is:
questions.questionHtml: A man invested a total of Rs.12,050 in two parts, one at 10% p.a. simple interest for 2 years and the other at the same rate at compound interest, interest being compounded annually, for the same time. The amounts he received from both the parts are equal. The sum (in Rs.) invested at the compound interest is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Total investment = Rs.12050

Rate of interest = 10% 

Time = 2 years 

Formulas used:

Simple Interest = Principal × Time × Rate/100 

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest 

In Compound Interest; Amount = Principal × (1 + R/100)n

Calculation:

Let the sum invested at compound interest be = y 

⇒ Sum invested at simple interest = 12050 - y 

As per the question;

(12050 - y) + (12050 - y) × 10/100 × 2 = y × (1 + 10/100)2

⇒ (12050 - y) [1 + 1/5] = y × 11/10 × 11/10 

⇒ (12050 - y) × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒ 12050 × 6/5 - y × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒14460 = 121y/100 + 6y/5

⇒ 14460 = (121y + 120y)/100 

⇒ 14460 = 241y/100 

⇒y = (14460 × 100)/241 

⇒ y = 6000 

∴ The sum invested on compound interest is Rs.6000.

Alternate MethodEquivalent rate of interest in the case of CI 

⇒ 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%

Let a and b be the sum invested on SI and CI.

a + (a × 2 × 10)/100 = b + (b × 21)/100

⇒ a/b = 121/120

(121 + 120) units = 12050

⇒ 241 units = 12050

⇒ 1 unit = 12050/241 = 50

The sum invested on CI = 120 units = 50 × 120

⇒ Rs. 6000

 The sum invested on compound interest is Rs.6000.

questions.question: A sum lent out at compound interest amounts to Rs. 1,250 in one year and to Rs. 1,458 in 3 years at a certain rate percentage p.a. What is the simple interest on the same sum for \(5\frac{2}{5}\) years at the same rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum lent out at compound interest amounts to Rs. 1,250 in one year and to Rs. 1,458 in 3 years at a certain rate percentage p.a. What is the simple interest on the same sum for \(5\frac{2}{5}\) years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
As we know,

A = P (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 1250 = P (1 + r/100)1          ---(1)

Again

⇒ 1458 = P (1 + r/100)3          ---(2)

From equation (1) and equation (2)

1458/1250 = [P (1 + r/100)3]/[P (1 + r/100)1]

⇒ 729/625 = (1 + r/100)2

⇒ √729/625 = 1 + r/100

⇒ 27/25 - 1 = r/100

⇒ r/100 = 2/25

⇒ r = 2/25 × 100

⇒ r = 8%

From equation (1)

1250 = P (1 + 8/100)

⇒ P = 1250 × 25/27

⇒ P = (1250 × 25)/27

Again,

Time = 27/5 and R = 8%

SI = Prt/100

SI = (1250 × 25 × 27 × 8)/(100 × 5 × 27)

SI = 500

Interest paid to R = 0.08P

questions.question: A certain sum becomes Rs. 13650 at 15% p.a. simple interest after 2 years. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 1 year at the same rate of interest, if the interest is compounded half yearly? (nearest to a Rs.)
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum becomes Rs. 13650 at 15% p.a. simple interest after 2 years. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 1 year at the same rate of interest, if the interest is compounded half yearly? (nearest to a Rs.)
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount = Rs. 13650

Rate of Interest = 15%

Time = 2 Years

Formula used:

S.I = PRT/100

Amount = Principal + S.I

Calculation:

Let the Principal be Rs. x

S.I = Rs. (13650 – x)

According to the question,

⇒ (x × 15 × 2)/100 = 13650 – x

⇒ 3x/10 = 13650 – x

⇒ 3x = 136500 – 10x

⇒ 13x = 136500

⇒ x = 10500

Now, if rate of interest is compounded half yearly, the interest becomes half and Time becomes twice

So, Rate of interest = 15% ÷ 2 = 7.5%

Time period = 1 × 2 = 2 years

Now, amount after 1 year = Rs. 10500 × (107.5/100)2

⇒ Rs. 12134.0625 ≈ Rs. 12134

∴ Amount becomes Rs. 12134 after 1 year if compounded half yearly

questions.question: Peter invested a certain sum of money in a scheme paying 10% simple interest per annum, while Rachel invested half of the sum that Peter invested in a scheme paying 10% interest per annum compounded annually. Also, while Peter invested for 2 years, Rachel invested for 3 years. If the difference in the interest earned by Peter and Rachel was Rs. 897, what was the sum that Rachel had invested?
questions.questionHtml: Peter invested a certain sum of money in a scheme paying 10% simple interest per annum, while Rachel invested half of the sum that Peter invested in a scheme paying 10% interest per annum compounded annually. Also, while Peter invested for 2 years, Rachel invested for 3 years. If the difference in the interest earned by Peter and Rachel was Rs. 897, what was the sum that Rachel had invested?
questions.solution:
Let's denote Peter's principal (the sum he invested) as (P) ⇒ SI = \(\frac{P\times 2\times10}{100}\) = \(\frac{P}{5}\)

Rachel's principal = (P/2) ⇒ CI = \( \frac{P}{2}[(1 + \frac{10}{100})^3 - 1]\) ⇒ CI = \( \frac{P}{2}[(\frac{11}{10})^3 - 1]\) = \( \frac{P}{2}[0.331]\)

Interest Difference = 897

\(\frac{P}{5}\) - \( \frac{P}{2}[0.331]\) = 897 ⇒ P = Rs. 26000

The sum that Rachel had invested =P/2 = 26000/2 =  Rs. 13,000.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,000 is invested for 15 months at 10% per annum compounded half yearly. What is the percentage gain, at the end of 15 months, correct to one decimal place?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 12,000 is invested for 15 months at 10% per annum compounded half yearly. What is the percentage gain, at the end of 15 months, correct to one decimal place?
questions.solution:
Suppose P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

Compound interest calculated half yearly = P(1 + (R/2)/100)2n – 1

Given,

Time = 1 year and 3 months

Amount = 12000(1 + 5/100)2 = 13230

Simple Interest = (13230 × 3/12 × 10)/100 = 330.75

Amount after 15 months = 13230 + 330.75 = Rs.13560.75

Percentage increase = (13560.75 – 12000) / (12000) × 100 = 13.0%

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹ 11,520 in 4 years at the rate of 15% p.a. simple interest. what will be the amount of the same sum in 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly (nearest to a ₹)?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum amounts to ₹ 11,520 in 4 years at the rate of 15% p.a. simple interest. what will be the amount of the same sum in 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly (nearest to a ₹)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount = ₹ 11,520 

T = 4 years, R = 15% p.a. simple interest

Concept Used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Where, P is principal, r is rate of interest 

If p be the principal, r be the rate of interest then the interest compounded 8 monthly then compound interest will be P x [(1 + r/100)3 - 1]

Calculation:

SI = PRT/100

= P x 15 x (4/100)

= 3P/5

Amount = P + SI

⇒ 11520 = P + 3P/5

⇒ P = 7200

Time = 3years (compounded 8 monthly)

Rate = 15/12 x 8 = 10%

CI = P x [(1 + r/100)3 - 1]

= 7200 x [(1 + 10/100)3 - 1]

= 2383

Amount = 7200 + 2383

= 9583

Therefore, the amount of the same sum in 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly is ₹9583

Confusion Points ⇒ 2 year =  3 × 8 months 

so here we use 3 year.

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of Rs. 8,000 at a certain rate per cent per annum for 3 years is Rs. 3,600. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum of Rs. 8,000 at a certain rate per cent per annum for 3 years is Rs. 3,600. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum after 2 years at the same rate, if the interest is compounded 8-monthly?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) = (3600 × 100) ÷ (8000 × 3) = 15% p.a.

For 8-monthly compounding, cycle rate = 15% × (8 ÷ 12) = 10% per 8 months.

Total time of 2 years = 24 months, which gives 24 ÷ 8 = 3 compounding cycles.

Amount after 3 cycles at 10% growth = 8000 × (11/10)3

Amount = 8000 × 1.331 = 10648.

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,648.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹8000

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹3600

Time for SI (T) = 3 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 3600 = (8000 × R × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 3600 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 15% per annum

⇒ The rate for an 8-monthly period = 15% × (8 ÷ 12) = 10%

⇒ Time duration = 2 years = 24 months

⇒ Number of 8-monthly cycles (n) = 24 ÷ 8 = 3

⇒ Total Amount = P(1 + R/100)n

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (1 + 10/100)3

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (11/10) × (11/10) × (11/10)

⇒ Total Amount = 8000 × (1331 ÷ 1000)

⇒ Total Amount = 8 × 1331 = 10648

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,648.

Additional Information

Effective Compounding Rate

When interest is compounded k-monthly, the applicable rate per cycle becomes R% × (k ÷ 12) and total cycles become Total Months ÷ k.

Compound vs Simple Interest Difference

For 2 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)2. For 3 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Frequencies

If compounded Half-yearly: Rate is halved, time cycles are doubled. If Quarterly: Rate becomes one-fourth, time cycles become four times.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of ₹ P at a rate of r% per annum for 3 years is Rs.11,250 and the compound interest on the same sum for 2 years at the same rate percent p.a. is ₹ 7,650. What is the value of P and r, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum of ₹ P at a rate of r% per annum for 3 years is Rs.11,250 and the compound interest on the same sum for 2 years at the same rate percent p.a. is ₹ 7,650. What is the value of P and r, respectively?
questions.solution:
SI for 1 year = 11,250 ÷ 3 = Rs 3,750, SI for 2 year = 2 × 3750 = Rs 7500

Difference between CI and SI for 2 year = 7650 - 7500 = Rs 150

P = \(SI\times 100\over {R\times T}\) ⇒ Rate % = \(150\over 3750\) × 100 = 4% 

⇒ Principal = \(3750\times 100\over {1\times4}\) = Rs 93,750

questions.question: The difference in compound interest on a certain sum at 10% p.a. for one year, when the interest is compounded half-yearly and yearly, is Rs. 88.80. What is the simple interest on the same sum for \(1\frac{2}{3}\) years at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: The difference in compound interest on a certain sum at 10% p.a. for one year, when the interest is compounded half-yearly and yearly, is Rs. 88.80. What is the simple interest on the same sum for \(1\frac{2}{3}\) years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in effective interest rate for 1 year = (5 × 5) / 100 = 0.25%.

0.25% of Sum = Rs. 88.80 ⇒ 100% of Sum (Principal) = 88.80 × 400 = Rs. 35,520.

Simple Interest for 12/3 (or 5/3) years = (35,520 × 10 × 5/3) / 100.

Required SI = 35,520 ÷ 6 = Rs. 5,920.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,920.

Alternate Method

Given: Rate (R) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 1 year, Difference in CI = Rs. 88.80.

Formula Used: CI = P[(1 + r/n)nt − 1]; SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

⇒ Case 1 (Yearly): CI1 = P × 10% = 0.10P

⇒ Case 2 (Half-yearly): Rate = 5%, Periods = 2; CI2 = P[(1 + 0.05)2 − 1] = 0.1025P

⇒ Difference = 0.1025P − 0.10P = 0.0025P

⇒ 0.0025P = 88.80 ⇒ P = 88.80 / 0.0025 = 35,520

⇒ For SI: T = 5/3 years, R = 10%

⇒ SI = (35,520 × 10 × 5/3) ÷ 100 = 35,520 × 50 ÷ 300

⇒ SI = 35,520 ÷ 6 = 5,920

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,920.

Additional Information

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 (R' = R/2) and the time is multiplied by 2 (n = 2T).

Difference for Two Periods

The difference between CI and SI for two periods is given by P × (R/100)2, where R is the rate per period.

Effective Rate Method

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%. This is useful for Compound Interest calculations.

questions.question: A borrowed a sum of Rs. 160000 from B at 10% per annum simple interest. At the same time he lent the same sum to C at the same rate on compound interest, compounded semi-annually for 2 years, Find the amount (in Rs.) earned by A in the whole transaction.
questions.questionHtml: A borrowed a sum of Rs. 160000 from B at 10% per annum simple interest. At the same time he lent the same sum to C at the same rate on compound interest, compounded semi-annually for 2 years, Find the amount (in Rs.) earned by A in the whole transaction.
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 160000

Rate = 10%

Time = 2 years

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P × (1 + r/100)t

CI = Amount –  Principal

When compound semi-annually, r' = r/2 and t' = 2 × t

Calculation:

According to the question

SI = (160000 × 10 × 2)/100

⇒ Rs. 32000

Now,

Compounded amount when compounded semi annually = P(1 + r/200)2 × t

Compounded amount = 160000[1 + 10/200)2 × 2

⇒ 160000(21/20)4

⇒ Rs. (160000 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20 × 21/20)

⇒ Rs. 194481

CI = Amount – Principal = (194481 – 160000)

⇒ Rs. 34481

Now, the amount earned by A in the whole transaction = CI – SI

⇒ (34481 – 32000)

⇒ Rs. 2481

∴ Required amount earned by A in the whole transaction is 2481

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years at the rate of 10% per annum is Rs. 2940. What will be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for \(1\frac{1}{2}\) years at the same rate when interest is compounded half-yearly (nearest to a rupee)?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a certain sum for \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years at the rate of 10% per annum is Rs. 2940. What will be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for \(1\frac{1}{2}\) years at the same rate when interest is compounded half-yearly (nearest to a rupee)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Simple interest = Rs. 2940

Time = \(3\frac{1}{2}\) years

Rate = 10%

Formula used:

S.I = (P × t × r)/100

C.I = P(1 + r/100)n - P

Calculation:

Let principal be P

According to the question,

2940 = (P × 3.5 × 10)/100

⇒ P = Rs. 8400

C.I = 8400(1 + 5/100)3 - 8400

⇒ 8400 × (21/20)3 - 8400

⇒ 8400 × 9261/8000 - 8400

⇒ 9724.05 - 8400

⇒ Rs. 1324.05 ≈ Rs. 1324

∴ Compound interest will be Rs. 1324

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs.291600 in 2 years and to Rs.314928 in 3 years on compound interest compounded annually. How much will be the simple interest (in Rs.) on Rs.40000 at the same rate for 2 years?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum amounts to Rs.291600 in 2 years and to Rs.314928 in 3 years on compound interest compounded annually. How much will be the simple interest (in Rs.) on Rs.40000 at the same rate for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount in 2 years = Rs.291600

Amount in 3 years = Rs.314928

Formula:

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time period

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)n - P

Amount = P(1 + R/100)n

Simple interest = PNR/100

Calculation:

⇒ 291600 = P(1 + R/100)2

⇒ 314928 = P(1 + R/100)3

⇒ 1.08 = (1 + R/100)

⇒ R = 8%

Rate of interest is 8% per annum.

Then,

Simple interest = 40000 × 8 × 2/100 = Rs.6400

∴ simple interest on Rs.40000 at the same rate for 2 years is Rs.6400.

questions.question: There is a 60% increase in an amount in 5 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on Rs. 6,250 for two years at the same rate of interest, when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.questionHtml: There is a 60% increase in an amount in 5 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on Rs. 6,250 for two years at the same rate of interest, when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:

A Simple Interest on a particular sum is 60% of the principle in 5 years.

Let P be the principle and R% is the rate of interest p.a.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest ( S.I ) = ( P× R× T )/ 100

Where P = Principle, R = Rate of interest, T = time period

Compound Interest ( C.I ) = P(1 + R/100)T – P

Where P = Principle, R = Rate of interest, T = time period

Calculations:

⇒ As from the given formula

  S.I for 5 years = 60%× P = P× R%× 5

⇒ R% = 60% / 5 = 12%      ____( 1 )

As 12% = ( +3/25) = 28/25

⇒ C.I = 6250( 1 + 12/100 )2 – 6250

(∵ Principle is given = Rs 6250 )

⇒ C.I = 6250 (28/25)2 – 6250 = 6250× 784/625 – 6250

( As 282 = 784, 252 = 625 )

C.I = 7840 – 6250 = Rs 1590

questions.question: A man invests Rs. 7,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 2 years and Rs. 10,000 at compound interest at the same rate for the same period, compounded annually. What will be the total interest and the total amount (in Rs.) respectively, on maturity?
questions.questionHtml: A man invests Rs. 7,000 at 8% per annum simple interest for 2 years and Rs. 10,000 at compound interest at the same rate for the same period, compounded annually. What will be the total interest and the total amount (in Rs.) respectively, on maturity?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sum = Rs.7000

Rate of interest = 8%

Time = 2 years

Formula:

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

SI = PNR/100

CI = P(1 + R/100)2 - P

Calculation:

SI = 7000 × 8 × 2/100 = Rs.1120

Amount after SI = 7000 + 1120 = Rs.8120

CI = 10000(1 + 8/100)2 - 10000 = Rs.1664

Amount after CI = 10000 + 1664 = Rs.11664

∴ Total amount after maturity = 8120 + 11664 = Rs.19784

Total interest after 2 years = 1120 + 1664 = Rs.2784

questions.question: Varun and Madhur invested Rs. 25,000 each in different schemes. Varun earned simple interest at 11% per annum, whereas Madhur earned compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually. Who received more interest after 2 years and how much?
questions.questionHtml: Varun and Madhur invested Rs. 25,000 each in different schemes. Varun earned simple interest at 11% per annum, whereas Madhur earned compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually. Who received more interest after 2 years and how much?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate of interest = 11%

Formula:

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time

Simple interest = PNR/100

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)n - P

Calculation:

SI earned by Varun = (25000 × 2 × 11)/100 = Rs.5500

Equivalent rate of interest for Madhur = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%

Compound interest for Madhur = 21% of 25000 = (25000 × 21)/100

⇒ Rs. 5250

Difference between interests = 5500 - 5250 = Rs.250

∴ Varun earned Rs.250 more interest than Madhur.

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 8,100. What would be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for the same period at 15% p. a., when the interest is compounded yearly? (nearest to Rs. 1)
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 8,100. What would be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for the same period at 15% p. a., when the interest is compounded yearly? (nearest to Rs. 1)
questions.solution:
Given:

R = 10%

T = 2 years

SI = Rs.8,100

R2 for CI = 15%

Formula Used:

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

A = P(1+ R/100)T

C.I. = A – P

Where, 

P → Principle

T → Time

R → Rate

A → Amount 

Calculation:

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 8,100 = (P × 2 × 10)/100

⇒ 8,100 = P/5

⇒ P = 5 × 8,100

⇒ P = 40,500

Now for C.I.

A = P(1+ R/100)T

⇒ A = 40,500(1 + 15/100)2 

⇒ A = 40,500(1 +3/20)2

⇒ A = 40,500(23/20)2 

⇒ A = 40,500 × (23/20) × (23/20)

⇒ A = 53561.25

CI = A – P

⇒ C.I. = 53561.25 – 40500 = Rs. 13,061.25 ≈ Rs. 13,061

∴ The required compound interest is Rs. 13,061

Alternate Method10% for 2 years = 20% of principle = 8100

⇒ 20P/100 = 8100

⇒ P = 40500

Equivalent rate of interest for 2 years = 15 + 15 + (15 × 15)/100 = 32.25%

C.I. = 32.25% of 40500

⇒ 32.25 × 40500 /100 =  Rs. 13061.25 ≈ Rs. 13061

∴ The required CI is Rs. 13061.

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and amounts to Rs. 7896 in 3 years on compound interest (compounding annually) at the same rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.questionHtml: A sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and amounts to Rs. 7896 in 3 years on compound interest (compounding annually) at the same rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

If the sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and Rs. 7896 in 3 years, the difference (Rs. 7896 - Rs. 6580 = Rs. 1316) would be the interest earned in the third year.

So, the interest for the third year, Rs. 1316, was obtained from the amount that was there at the end of two years, which is Rs. 6580.

Interest for third year = Sum after 2 years × annual interest rate

1316 = 6580 × r

Solving this equation for r gives us:

r = 1316/6580 × 100 = 20%

So, the annual rate of interest is 20%.

questions.question: If the difference between the compounded interest and simple interest at 17% on a sum of money for 2 years (compounded annually) is Rs. 433.50, then compound interest (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the compounded interest and simple interest at 17% on a sum of money for 2 years (compounded annually) is Rs. 433.50, then compound interest (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

R = 17%

Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years = Rs. 433.50

Formula used:

Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years = P × R/100 × R/100

Compound interest = P × (1 + R/100)T - P

Calculation:

Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years = P × R/100 × R/100

⇒ 433.50 = P × 17/100 × 17/100

⇒ 43350 × 100 = P × 289

⇒ P = 4335000/289 = 15000

Compound interest = P × (1+R/100)T - P

⇒ 15000 × (1 + 17/100)2 - 15000

⇒ 15000 × [(117/100 × 117/100) – 1]

⇒ 15000 × (13689 – 10000)/10000

⇒ (15 × 3689)/10

⇒ Rs. 5533.5

∴ Compound interest for two years is Rs. 5533.5 

Alternate Method

2 years Effective rate for S.I. = RT 

⇒ 17 × 2 = 34% 

2 years Effective rate for C.I = 2R + R2/100 

⇒ 2 × 17 + 172/100

⇒ 34 + 2.89 = 36.89% 

Difference in rates = 36.89% – 34% = 2.89% 

Now, 2.89% = 433.50 

Here we have to find C.I so = (433.50/2.89) × 36.89 = 5533.5 

∴ The compound interest for two years is Rs. 5533.5

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 5 years at the rate of 10% per annum is half the compound interest on Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at the rate of 10% per annum, interest compounded yearly. The sum placed on simple interest is:

Calculation:

⇒ 5000(1 + 10/100)2 – 5000

⇒ 5000(110/100)2 – 5000

⇒ (5000 × 11/10 × 11/10) – 5000

⇒ P = Rs. (525 × 100)/50

⇒ P = Rs. 1050

questions.question: If the difference between the compound interest compounded annually and the simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% per annum is Rs. 279, then the sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the compound interest compounded annually and the simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% per annum is Rs. 279, then the sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate = 10%

Time = 3 years

The difference between the CI and SI = Rs. 279

Formula used:

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

CI = A – P

Calculation:

Let Principal be x

SI = (x × 10 × 3)/100

⇒ 3x/10

Now,

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ x(1 + 10/100)3

⇒ [x(100 + 10)/100]3

⇒ [x(110/100)3]

⇒ (x × 11/10 × 11/10 × 11/10)

⇒ 1331x/1000

Now,

CI = A – P

⇒ CI = (1331x/1000 – x)

⇒ (1331x – 1000x)/1000

⇒ 331x/1000

The difference between the CI and SI = Rs. 279

⇒ 331x/1000 – 3x/10 = 279

⇒ (331x – 300x)/1000 = 279

⇒ 31x/1000 = 279

⇒ x = (9 × 1000)

⇒ Rs. 9000

Shortcut Trick

Calculation:

⇒ \(\frac{P× 10^2 × (300 + 10)}{100^3 }\) = 279

⇒ P = (279 × 1003)/(100 × 310)

⇒ P = 9000

questions.question: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% p.a. is Rs. 558, then the sum is:
questions.questionHtml: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% p.a. is Rs. 558, then the sum is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For 10% rate (1/10) over 3 years, let Principal = 103 = 1000 units.

The difference (D) between CI and SI is given by the ratio: D = 3R + 1 (where R is the denominator 10).

⇒ Difference = 3(10) + 1 = 31 units.

Given 31 units = ₹558 ⇒ 1 unit = 558 ÷ 31 = 18.

Sum (Principal) = 1000 units × 18 = ₹18,000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹18,000.

Alternate Method

Given: Rate (R) = 10% per annum, Time (T) = 3 years, Difference (D) = ₹558.

Formula Used: Difference (D) = P(R/100)2 × [(300 + R) / 100]

⇒ 558 = P × (10/100)2 × [(300 + 10) / 100]

⇒ 558 = P × (1/10)2 × (310 / 100)

⇒ 558 = P × (1/100) × (31/10)

⇒ 558 = P × (31 / 1000)

⇒ P = (558 × 1000) ÷ 31

⇒ P = 18 × 1000

⇒ P = 18,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹18,000.

Additional Information

Difference for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)2.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n, where n is the number of years. CI = A − P.

Effective Rate Method

For 10% rate for 3 years, the effective SI is 30% and the effective CI is 33.1%. The difference is 3.1% of the Principal.
